title: Normalized tensor structures on existing pro-etale section-module functors
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the pulled-back coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the fixed section equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the actual section-ring coefficient map, module direct image, tensor-formula inverse image, specified adjunction, open extension and geometric composition maps already constructed in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. For the relative tensors [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], normalize the internal and section-module direct-image lax tensor structures by the local pure-tensor pairing. Their uniquely determined unit maps are the regular-module coefficient maps. Define inverse-image oplax structures as their adjunction mates, with their strong structures supplied by the invertibility of the local scalar-extension tensor and unit formulas. Internal pullback preserves flat modules. Use the unique local-pure-tensor ordinary tensor comparison and the unique scalar-section regular-unit comparison on the local pure tensors of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Define the signed direct-sum total comparison by its value on every summand of fixed total degree. The exactness and additivity prerequisites of the specified functors are named construction lemmas, including exact inverse image, exact open extension, and preservation of homology by the section equivalence. The internal functors and open extension are those of [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star], and [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].

proof.text: Keep the operations-data aliases. The internal-section tensor theorem supplies the normalized ordinary tensor/unit comparisons. Precomposing two tensor candidates with its inverse reduces uniqueness to the sheaf-bilinear universal property; scalar sections determine the regular-unit comparison.

Apply the ringed-direct-image pairing lemma with $v(U)=U\times_YX$ and the retained coefficient map. Its scalar action is precisely the retained direct image, so it supplies the unique section-module lax structure, including the coefficient-map unit.

Operations transport identifies the retained adjunction with the canonical scalar-extension adjunction on these geometric sites. The canonical-unit lemma supplies its insertion formula (the coefficient map is invertible). Apply the ringed tensor-mate lemma, then invertible-oplax-to-strong, to obtain the section pullback strong structure with exactly its specified mate maps.

Apply monoidal adjunction transport to $E_Y,E_X$ with the ordinary comparisons of Step 1. Operations transport supplies the functor and adjunction identifications; its direct-image comparison is identity on sections. Thus local pure tensors and regular-unit maps are unchanged, giving the unique normalized internal lax structure and invertible mate maps. Apply invertible-oplax-to-strong internally. Any normalized candidate has the same images by bilinear universality, hence is equal by faithfulness.

source.place: Tags 00YV and 03EK; fixed monoidal comparisons and specified adjunction identifications

proof.text: Exact internal pullback and exact open extension transport through the additive exact section equivalences. Kernels, images and cokernels then transport, hence so does homology. Direct image adds maps sectionwise, hence preserves sums and zero; pullback and extension are additive through these identifications. Tensor maps with a zero factor vanish on pure tensors and hence vanish by bilinear universality, also internally by faithfulness.

The coefficient isomorphism identifies internal scalar extension with restriction along $\alpha_f^{-1}$. Apply inverse-image-module-flat to this inverse and conjugate by extension-along-iso. Isomorphic tensor functors have the same exactness tests, so the actual internal pullback preserves flat modules.

The internal-section theorem supplies a signed-total comparison whose summand maps are Step 1's unique ordinary comparisons. In degree $n$, the section equivalence preserves the coproduct indexed by $p+q=n$; its inclusions therefore determine maps out of that degree. This proves uniqueness degreewise and hence on chain maps, including unbounded complexes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N7-2d7ad77dc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX: the re-split order is now carried out and the mathematics is sound; the only change is a wrong source locator on the item. The 2026-10-21 repair note asked for a finer split, and this delivery does it. The parent's statement is unchanged and its proof is now a 7-step assembly of 2526 characters, every step under 800. It adds three new unsplit, statement-only nodes, each searched with LeanFinder, Loogle and grep; LeanSearch was rate-limited for two of them and is recorded as unavailable, as B7 permits. There is no cycle (closure of 423 nodes, item not in it), proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the live node is still the old version. I read every step against the cited statements. Step 1 gets uniqueness from lem-pe plus the lem-pc bilinear bijection. Step 2: the retained direct image is exactly the P of the pairing lemma with v(U)=U×_Y X. Step 3: the unit hypothesis is supplied by lem-pod-canonical-module-adjunction-unit, with c invertible because alpha_f is an isomorphism (sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms). Step 4: E_Y and E_X are strong monoidal by lem-pe, and beta and gamma with their units and counits come from operations-transport. Step 6: f*_int ≅ mapModComap(alpha^-1), which is the direction new-proetale-inverse-image-module-flat requires. Step 7 is unique by the coproduct property, including unbounded complexes. The pairing lemma is true: mu is balanced over c_U, and the unit is forced to e=c by the left unit law at S and 1, also in the zero ring. The mate lemma is true for any alpha: the transposes agree on m⊗n, and the scalar formula and unit inverse are correct. In the transport lemma the Hom-bijection condition type-checks; the lax structure is the full-faithful preimage, and invertibility is reflected by the fully faithful F. None of the three is a duplicate: the lem-sc Gamma(X,-) lax/oplax nodes, lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates, lem-pur-independent-ringed-tensorator-existence and def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal all say something different. No SGA source is used. The six declared tool_uses are generic module/tensor/equivalence black boxes, and I accept them. Fix: the item's source.place cited sites-cohomology.tex 06YN for the signed total tensor, but 06YN is the definition of K-flat; it should be 012Z (homology-definition-associated-simple-complex), as Step 7 already says. The corrected whole file is at fixes/dag/nodes/sec-poincare-duality/def-pd-proetale-section-module-functors.json; nothing else in it changed. Also, the report promises complete proofs in words for the new nodes but gives only their sources; per the human's note the next stage-1 worker writes those proofs.
